subject: PrivCP operator bridge & delegated-admin cutover checklist
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@fintechcorp.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: security@fintechcorp.com, DevOps Team <devops@fintechcorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: PrivCP access model: delegated operator + SCIM sync questions

Sofia — thanks again for running the demo yesterday. A few follow-ups from our side as we prepare our network/integration sprint next week:

1) We need a clear pattern for cross-account operator roles so our cloud admins don't have to share long-lived keys. Can Redwood support assume-role style access from our AWS org and equivalent in GCP?

2) For SAML assertions, our IdP (Okta) can send group claims but we need guidance on mapping Okta group -> Redwood role -> customer project RBAC. Is there an example mapping?

3) SCIM: we plan to push groups for operator teams. Does Redwood support group scoping (e.g., limit SCIM sync to a subset of groups and filter by attribute)?

We attached our proposed group list and would like to run a short connectivity test during your canary cutover. Also we need to confirm audit log forwarding (CloudWatch/Stackdriver -> our SIEM).

Thanks — Alex

--
Alex Martinez
Head of Infrastructure, FinTechCorp
alex.martinez@fintechcorp.com

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivCP access model: delegated operator + SCIM sync questions

Alex — great questions, and yes we can support the patterns you described. High-level answers below; I'll follow with an internal checklist and a proposed canary window.

1) Cross-account operator roles: Redwood supports AWS AssumeRole and GCP Service Account impersonation. We recommend creating a short-lived operator role in your account (AdminAssumeRole-FinTechCorp) that our bridge service can assume with STS. For GCP, create a workload-identity pool binding to allow Redwood's token broker to impersonate a service account. We'll provide a terraform snippet you can apply.

2) SAML group mapping: We support SAML group attributes and can map assertion groups to fine-grained Redwood roles. See attached SCIM mapping proposal for an example (Operator -> rwd-operator, Oncall -> rwd-oncall). We'll also add a fallback mapping so users without groups land in a constrained "guest-operator" role during cutover.

3) SCIM scoping & filtering: Yes — our SCIM connector supports group filtering by attribute and prefix. We recommend scoping by an attribute (e.g., companyResource=true) and a blacklist of groups you don't want synced. We can run a dry-run sync to validate membership before writeback.

Audit log forwarding: we support log export to S3/Cloud Storage or direct syslog collector. For SIEM ingestion, customers often forward from a central aggregator. We'll verify event-time retention and link to your SIEM team during the canary.

I'll attach a short cutover checklist and runbook excerpts — proposing a Tuesday morning canary (11/2) for a small operator group.

Best,
Sofia

--
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-28T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivCP access model: delegated operator + SCIM sync questions

Sofia / Jasmine — putting together the cutover checklist and terraform snippets. Notes for the team: 

- AWS AssumeRole snippet: create role with limited session duration (15m), require MFA if possible, trust policy limited to Redwood broker principal. Add CloudTrail read-only to see assume events.
- GCP: create workload identity pool, add trust relationship to Redwood service account. Use short-lived tokens and ensure IAM Conditions block token usage outside the customer VPC's CIDR (if they require).
- SCIM: default to read-only patch operations on first sync. Provide a "preview" mode that returns affected users/groups.
- SAML mapping: implement a two-tier mapping: primary group -> redwood-role; secondary attribute (project_id) -> project-scoped role binding.

Attachments: privcp-scim-group-mapping-v1.xlsx (mapping sample), operator-bridge-canary-runbook.pdf (draft runbook).

I'll create RDWD-7832 for the terraform deliverable; jasmine, can you capture any security review ask?

-ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-29T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivCP access model: delegated operator + SCIM sync questions

Ben — quick notes for the security review standing up: 

- Auditability: ensure every assumed-role action emits CloudTrail/Stackdriver logs with a unique session id we can correlate to Redwood request ids. We'll require log forwarding to their SIEM before full cutover.
- Key management: no long-lived keys stored in customer account; our broker issues ephemeral credentials and we rotate any broker certs on customer rotation schedule. Document cert rotation endpoint for them.
- Least privilege: operator roles default to 'operator:read,exec' and require an explicit "elevate" action (timeboxed) for destructive ops. This elevate request creates a traceable approval entry.

Also flagging that we need FinTechCorp's Okta attribute schema to finalize mapping. Alex — can your IdP team share the SAML attribute names (groups, project_id, department) and SCIM base endpoint?

-jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@fintechcorp.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: security@fintechcorp.com, DevOps Team <devops@fintechcorp.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-30T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivCP access model: delegated operator + SCIM sync questions

Thanks — this looks good. Our IdP team attached the Okta attribute dump and SCIM base URL (see attachment). We're happy with the proposed canary plan on 2026-11-02 10:00 PT for a 30-minute window; we'll limit to two operator groups (Platform-Ops and Oncall).

A couple of requests before we start: 
- Please share the terraform snippets and the canary runbook link in Confluence (we prefer company-owned links).
- Confirm the fallback policy: if SCIM write fails during the canary, Redwood should not create or modify roles; only preview results and preserve existing mappings.

If you can confirm those, we'll schedule the internal ticket and make our network team available for the connectivity test.

Appreciate the quick turn — Alex

--
Alex Martinez
Head of Infrastructure, FinTechCorp
